answers.q1: Ruby with Bundler (Rake is the task runner). The repo holds three gems: the root `sinatra` gem, `rack-protection/` and `sinatra-contrib/`. Install the root dependencies with `bundle install`. The root Gemfile pulls in the other two via `path:`. CI also runs `bundle install` inside `sinatra-contrib`, which has its own Gemfile. To match that, run `bundle install && (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install) && (cd rack-protection && bundle install)`.
answers.q2: There is no single command. CI runs three suites, one per gem: `bundle exec rake && (cd rack-protection && bundle exec rake) && (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake)`. The root `bundle exec rake` is the Minitest suite and is the default `test` task. The two `cd` calls run RSpec.
answers.q4: CI does not run any lint or formatting check. `.github/workflows/test.yml` only runs the three `bundle exec rake` suites. The repo's own lint command, from AGENTS.md, is `bundle exec rubocop`. It uses `.rubocop.yml`, which targets Ruby 2.7 and excludes `test/`, `rack-protection/` and `sinatra-contrib/`.
answers.q5: No vendored source is committed. These are generated or ignored by `.gitignore`: `pkg/` (built gems and tarballs), `coverage/`, `doc/` (including `doc/api`, which `yardoc` generates), `.yardoc`, `.bundle`, `vendor/`, `*.gem` and `*.lock` (Gemfile.lock). Don't hand-edit these. The `VERSION` file is also tied to release tasks. `rake release:commit_version` rewrites the `version.rb` files from it, so change the version through that workflow rather than editing the `version.rb` files directly.
